questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase your stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without enough tread also increase the chance of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you not to enter the road or driveway from your direction. If you see this sign, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: It begins to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is too heavy and you cannot see well, drive to the shoulder and stop until it clears up.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic signal?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off before you go.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other cars. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the car back onto the road.
Speed up and slowly steer back onto the road.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently apply the brakes and slowly turn the wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes and slowly turn the wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep driving with your wheels off the road and slow down by gently braking. When it is safe, turn the wheel to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply or try to force the car back onto the road.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights or gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Some railroad crossings do not have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a car slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and the road. Low tire pressure or worn treads increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: How are bicycles treated on the road?

options.text: They must always yield to motor vehicles.
They do not have to follow traffic rules.
They are not a concern for drivers.
They have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Motor vehicle drivers should respect the rights of bicycle riders.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in school zones?
questions.explanation: In Florida, fines are doubled for violations in school zones. You may also face civil penalties up to $1,000 and be required to complete a driving school course.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when approaching them from behind. On hills with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction you must drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something back to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get out of the aggressive driver's way. Trying to get even makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross safely. Be alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: At night, it is hardest to see:
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other objects on the road.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry, you should:
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, stay away from them. Don't make eye contact or use gestures that could provoke them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: To make sure your health does not cause unsafe driving, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular checkups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and only drive if it is safe.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your mirrors to make sure no one is passing you. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: If someone drinks alcohol, what will help them feel normal again?
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol on a person.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking their rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before you reach the intersection. Watch for traffic and pedestrians. Turn only when your path is clear.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must show:
questions.explanation: You must carry and show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when stopped. All three documents are required by law.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a last-minute turn. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: If you miss your turn or exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Continue driving until you find the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you find the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway is illegal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. In this case, the road curves to the left. There may be several of these signs through the curve.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This circular sign indicates a railroad crossing ahead. It warns drivers to watch for trains.

questions.question: If your tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, do not slam the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Gradually slow down by releasing the accelerator. Once you are going very slowly, brake lightly and pull off the road to a safe area.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A roadway with rules about stereo volume.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on each side, in the rear, and in front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots when changing lanes. Look over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.
